title: Finance: Investments, Loans and Inflation
summary: Comparing investment options, compound interest calculated monthly and annually, loan repayments and the real cost of credit, and the effect of inflation on savings and prices.

notes.text: When comparing investments, consider the **interest rate**, how often interest is **compounded**, any **fees**, how long the money is **locked in**, and the **risk**.

notes.title: Worked example 1: comparing two accounts
notes.problem: R20 000 is invested for 2 years. Option A: 8% p.a. simple interest. Option B: 7,8% p.a. compounded monthly. Which gives more?

notes.text: Loans and the real cost of credit
A loan's **total cost** = all instalments + fees. Lenders quote an interest rate, but initiation fees, monthly service fees and credit life insurance add to the real cost.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: A personal loan of R30 000 is repaid with 36 instalments of R1 290, plus a R1 200 initiation fee. How much does the loan cost in total, and how much is the cost of credit?
steps: Cost of credit: R47 640 − R30 000 = R17 640
notes.answer: R47 640 in total; R17 640 is the cost of credit

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Loan repayment tables (e.g. 'monthly repayment per R1 000 borrowed') are often given. Multiply by the number of thousands borrowed, e.g. R12,35 per R1 000 for R450 000 gives 450 × R12,35 = R5 557,50.
If prices rise by more than the interest you earn, your savings lose **buying power**. The **real** return is roughly the interest rate minus the inflation rate.

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: Savings earn 4% p.a. while inflation is 6% p.a. What happens to the buying power of R10 000 after one year?
steps: Goods costing R10 000 now cost R10 600.
The savings buy less than before: buying power fell by about 2%.
